text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong, Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew and nine other members of Singapore's ruling People's Action Party obtain worldwide injunction to prevent opposition figure Tang Liang Hong from disposing of his assets if he has to pay for damages and legal costs in their defamation suits against him.
- United States must use balanced approach in its dealings with China, U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright says.
- Suzhou Singapore International School, which offers Singapore's bilingual educational curriculum to expatriate children, plans to start tuition classes for lower secondary school students.
- Mother reports son to police for stealing Singapore $200 from family maid.
- Four million shares offered to public by semiconductor leadframe maker Jade Technologies Singapore 189 times subscribed.
- Trading in menswear maker and retailer Orlando Holdings Bhd restricted by Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange after share price rockets up five ringgit or 25 percent to 25 ringgit.

- Singapore government sets aside plot of land in Tuas for pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies, a move which could see investments of about S$1 billion eventually, Economic Development Board says.
- Telekom Malaysia Bhd could lose its monopoly on fixed line telecommunications earlier than expected.
- Singapore-based investors in U.S. equities take profit and divest US$2.1 billion in third quarter 1996 after making net purchases for five straight quarters.
- Malaysia's plans to have a shorter settlement period for share transactions will be announced this year, according to Salleh Mahid, president of the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange.
- Cellular phone firm Globe Telecom will continue to lose money this year but company is sure to post profits next year.
- Uraco Holdings plans to raise S$53.7 million through a proposed issue of warrants, floating rate notes and inverse floating rate notes.
